new: The address of the latest published GRS schema; every document holds the same address.
note: is published -> "published" as an adjective

new: The UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the shape of this schema last changed.
The build time, in UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ), of the GRS build that wrote this file. This value is only for debugging; to check whether a file is readable, use schemaVersion.
note: when the build was made -> "the build time" (no actor named for making a build)

new: The data that GRS exports to MSPDI, and the data that only GRS uses.
Same as MSPDI Project.
Same as MSPDI Calendars.
Same as MSPDI Tasks, except that Task.parentTaskUid and Task.siblingOrder give the WBS tree. GRS makes ID, OutlineLevel, OutlineNumber and Summary from that tree each time GRS writes MSPDI.
Same as MSPDI Resources.
Same as MSPDI Assignments.

The task groups; GRS shows each one as one row in both the Task Group Panel and the Task Group Area. taskGroupMembers says which tasks each task group holds. On reading an MSPDI file, GRS makes the task groups from the WBS.
Which task group each task belongs to: one entry per task, from taskUid to taskGroupId.
How GRS draws each task (shape, colors and outline width): exactly one entry per task.

One record per task that came from an imported MSPDI file: which file and which task in that file, so that a later import of the same file updates that task instead of adding a copy. A task made in GRS has no record.
note: made in GRS read as an adjective participle

new: The earlier plan: a saved copy of earlier task dates. GRS matches the copy to the current tasks by uid and draws the copy as an outline over the current tasks for comparison.
note: The plan as it was before -> "The earlier plan" (same wording as isBaselineVisible)

new: Comment boxes in the Task Group Area. Each comment box points at a task, a highlight box or a free point.
note: chart -> Task Group Area (01-04 near line 5590 places comment boxes in the Task Group Area); doubt: Schedule Canvas if a comment box may sit outside the Task Group Area

new: Highlight boxes: rectangles in the Task Group Area that mark a range of days over a range of task groups. GRS draws each highlight box with a frame, a fill or both.
How GRS draws the document when the document opens. GRS always writes the keys that always have a value.

Display scale of the drawing in the Schedule Canvas, in percent: at 100 GRS draws every ...Px value as that many CSS pixels, at 50 at half size. This value scales shapes and text together and does not change the App Header, the Command Palette or the browser zoom.
note: schedule drawing -> "drawing in the Schedule Canvas"; doubt: does the scale also cover the Task Group Panel (taskGroupPanelWidthPx says yes)

new: Text size step of the schedule: small, medium or large, which are 7.5, 8.75 and 10 CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. The document opens at this step; a reader who changes the step edits the document.

Width of one calendar day on the time axis, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. When GRS fits the schedule to the window, GRS sets this value so that the whole schedule fits the width of the window.
note: flag: "Fit to screen" is in neither glossary nor spec (spec FR-055 says 全体表示; grs-commands.schema.json says "the Fit button") -> "fits the schedule to the window"; "width of the screen" -> "width of the window"; flag: "time axis" kept as plain words (no glossary name; Time Ruler is the nearest)

new: Vertical size of the task figures, as a ratio to the default size. 1 is the default size; 2 draws Plan Bars, Actual Bars and Name Labels twice as tall.
note: task name labels -> Name Labels (U-7); flag: "task figures" kept as plain words (no glossary name)

new: How deep task groups with treeState auto open. A top-level task group is depth 1. With value N, task groups down to depth N are open, so GRS shows rows down to depth N + 1; 0 shows only the top-level task groups, closed.
Where the view starts when the document opens: notDecided lets GRS choose, placed gives the day at the left edge and the task group at the top edge.
note: flag: "view" (here and D027, D029, D034) kept as a plain word; the glossary has no name for the scrolled view

new: notDecided: no person has chosen a place yet, and GRS chooses one when GRS opens the document; placed: the other keys give the place.
The day at the left edge of the view.
Where the left edge falls inside leftEdgeDay, as a part of that day; 0 is the start of the day.
The task group at the top edge of the view. When that task group is deleted, scrollPosition becomes notDecided.
note: kept passive "is deleted" (a person, an AI or GRS itself may delete the task group)

new: Where the top edge falls inside that task group, as a part of the step of the task group (the row height in the Task Group Area plus the gap below), not in pixels; 0 is the top of the row.
note: its band height -> "the row height in the Task Group Area" (the row of the task group)

new: The span of days, firstDay to lastDay (both included), that fitting the schedule to the window and PNG and SVG export show instead of the whole schedule when isFixed is true. Absent means no fit span.
note: flag: "Fit to screen" -> "fitting the schedule to the window" (see D022); "picture export" -> "PNG and SVG export"

new: The first day of the fit span (included), in the time zone that GRS shows the Schedule Canvas in (viewTimeZone).
note: chart -> Schedule Canvas

new: The last day of the fit span; the fit span includes the column of that day.
When true, fitting the schedule to the window and PNG and SVG export show the fit span instead of the whole schedule. Opening the document does not move the view.
note: flag: "Fit to screen" -> "fitting the schedule to the window" (see D022)

new: The time zone that the Time Ruler and the shown date-times use: sameAsScheduleData follows project.scheduleDataTimeZone, fixed uses the offset given here.
note: given here read as an adjective participle

new: sameAsScheduleData: show the schedule data time zone, and follow the schedule data time zone when that time zone changes; fixed: show the offset given here.
The UTC offset that GRS shows the Schedule Canvas in.
note: chart -> Schedule Canvas

new: Up to four extra clocks. While GRS shows the time of day, GRS shows each extra clock as one more row under the Time Ruler.
The UTC offset of this extra clock.
Whether this clock is the standard-time or the daylight-time zone of the offset of this clock. This value picks the zone name that GRS shows; GRS uses the offset itself all year.
Whether GRS shows the time of day on the Schedule Canvas; the stored date-times keep their time either way. A new document starts with false.
note: chart -> Schedule Canvas

new: Whether GRS shows Plan Bars, apart from isActualVisible. A new document starts with true.
Whether GRS shows the planned dates to the right of each Name Label. A new document starts with false.
Whether GRS shows Actual Bars, apart from isPlanVisible. A new document starts with true.
Whether GRS shows the Percent Complete Label of each task. A new document starts with false.
Whether GRS draws the earlier plan (baselineTasks) over the current tasks. A new document starts with false.
Whether GRS draws the Progress Line: the line from the status date through the progress point of each task. A new document starts with false.
Whether GRS draws Progress Markers and Resume Icons; while GRS shows Delay Diagnostics, GRS draws the Progress Markers even when this value is false. A new document starts with true.
note: flag: "Delay Diagnostics" kept (a function name, not in T-103; the window is the Delay Diagnostics Report)

new: Whether GRS draws Dependency Lines. A new document starts with true.
Whether GRS shows the Assignee Label of each task. A new document starts with false.
Whether GRS draws vertical Date Grid Lines. A new document starts with false.
Whether GRS draws the Group Grid Lines between task groups, in the Task Group Area and in the Task Group Panel. A new document starts with true.
note: lines between task groups -> Group Grid Lines (U-18)

new: up stacks the tasks of a task group so that the tasks climb to a goal at the upper right; down stacks them so that the tasks descend to a goal at the lower right. A new document starts with up.
note: the chart climbs -> "the tasks climb" (the chart drawn by the tasks; Task Group Area dropped for length)

new: Whether the theme is monochrome. A new document starts with false.
Width of the Task Group Panel, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100.
Whether the number taskGroupPanelWidthPx, instead of a drag of the Panel Divider, sets the width of the Task Group Panel. A new document starts with false.
note: panel border -> Panel Divider (U-24)

new: The state of the head of the Task Group Panel (level 0), above all top-level task groups. collapsed draws no task group at all. A new document starts with auto.
The Pinned Task Groups: task groups that stay together at the top of the Task Group Area, to compare them with task groups far away. Absent means no pinned task group.
note: flag: the pinned "band" has no glossary name; dropped, place kept as the top of the Task Group Area (01-04 LM-23); "pinned" read as an adjective

new: How GRS shows the three tables: the Search Panel, the Delay Diagnostics Report and the Resource List.
How GRS shows the tables of the Search Panel: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.
Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while the schedule filter is on, GRS draws in the Task Group Area only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.
note: the chart draws -> "GRS draws in the Task Group Area"

new: The tasks whose row has a check in the show column of this table. Absent means no row has a check.
note: is checked -> "has a check"

new: The column filters of the Search Panel tables (the task table and the comment box table), one per filtered column, by the column names of those tables. Absent means no column has a filter.
note: is filtered -> "has a filter"

new: How GRS sorts this table. Absent means the default order.
How GRS shows the Delay Diagnostics Report table: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.
Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while the schedule filter is on, GRS draws in the Task Group Area only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.
note: the chart draws -> "GRS draws in the Task Group Area"

new: The tasks whose row has a check in the show column of this table. Absent means no row has a check.
note: is checked -> "has a check"

new: The column filters of the Delay Diagnostics Report table, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column has a filter.
note: is filtered -> "has a filter"

new: How GRS sorts this table. Absent means the default order.
How GRS shows the Resource List table: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.
Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while the schedule filter is on, GRS draws in the Task Group Area only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.
note: the chart draws -> "GRS draws in the Task Group Area"

new: The resources whose row has a check in the show column of this table. Absent means no row has a check.
note: is checked -> "has a check"

new: Whether the (no assignee) row of the Resource List has a check. A new document starts with false.
note: is checked -> "has a check"

new: The column filters of the Resource List table, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column has a filter.
note: is filtered -> "has a filter"

new: How GRS sorts this table. Absent means the default order.
The stamp of the document: the time of the last change and of the last save, and who wrote the document last.
note: was saved -> "the last save" (no actor named)

new: The change log: notes that people or an AI write about changes to the document, oldest first. A new entry goes at the end.
note: New entries are added -> "A new entry goes" (no actor named)
